s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation

differentials: malignant melanoma of the lacrimal sac

shortlist.label: orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: left orbital pain, edematous and hyperemic left eyelids, and diffuse limitation in extraocular movements

shortlist.label: optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: visual acuity of 20/400 OS and acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

shortlist.label: dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: several months of epiphora and left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast

shortlist.label: orbital abscess
shortlist.why_kept: left-sided lacrimal sac abscess and postseptal fat stranding on CT with contrast

shortlist.label: cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: proptosis, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation, although not directly mentioned, is a possible complication of orbital cellulitis or abscess

raw.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast, increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT, and acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While there is edema and hyperemia, the key finding of an abscess on imaging studies points more specifically to an orbital abscess.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: The primary issue is the abscess and its complications, not isolated optic nerve inflammation.

rejected.label: dacryocystitis
rejected.why: Although there's a history of epiphora and a lacrimal sac abscess, the patient had no prior dacryocystitis, and the current issue is more severe and involves the orbit.

rejected.label: cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: There's no mention of specific findings that would indicate cavernous sinus thrombosis, such as bilateral eye involvement or specific neurologic deficits.
